  mode. It should detect text wrapped in triple quotes """text""" and render it 
   as a styled block - similar to how backtick code blocks work natively.       
  You'll have to write a main.js file, a manifest.json file, and a styles.css   
  file.

● The plugin is ready. Here's what was built:

  3 files created:

  - manifest.json — plugin metadata Obsidian needs to load it
  - styles.css — styles the rendered block (left accent border, secondary
  background, matches your theme via CSS vars)
  - main.js — the plugin logic

  How it works:

  The main.js uses CodeMirror 6's ViewPlugin + Decoration.replace() to scan the
  document for """...""" patterns on every view update, then replaces the
  matched range with a styled DOM widget in live preview. Key behavior:

  - Cursor-aware: when your cursor is inside a triple-quote block, it falls back
   to raw text so you can edit it normally — exactly like how Obsidian handles
  bold/italic
  - Multi-line: works across newlines since it scans the full doc string
  - Theme-compatible: uses Obsidian's CSS variables so it adapts to light/dark
  themes automatically

  To enable it:
  1. Go to Settings → Community Plugins → turn off Restricted mode if needed
  2. Enable "Triple Quote Blocks" in the installed plugins list
  3. Reload Obsidian if it doesn't appear (Ctrl+R)

❯ yeah, you got it exactly right. I tried using shift+enter assuming it would   
  insert a new line but it didn't.                                              

● The issue is a CodeMirror 6 limitation: Decoration.replace without block: true
   only works within a single line. Multi-line spans need block: true and their
  range aligned to full line boundaries.

● Reload the plugin (Settings → Community Plugins → disable then re-enable, or
  Ctrl+R to restart Obsidian). Both forms will now work:

  """same line text"""

  """
  multi
  line
  text
  """

  The leading/trailing newlines in the multi-line form are stripped, so both
  render identically. Use regular Enter (not Shift+Enter) to add lines inside
  the block — Obsidian's Shift+Enter inserts a <br> soft break which is a
  different character and won't affect the triple-quote detection.

● The key change: ViewPlugin → StateField. CM6 enforces that block decorations
  may only live in a StateField (because block-level changes affect layout in
  ways that need to be coordinated at the state level, not the view level). The
  logic is otherwise identical — StateField.update gets tr.docChanged and
  tr.selection the same way ViewPlugin.update did.

  Reload the plugin and both forms should now work without errors.

❯ kind of a non-issue, but when I click on the triple quote block it doesn't    
  move my keyboard cursor to the inside of that block. Is there any way you can 
   fix this? Also, when my keyboard cursor is above the block and I pressed the 
   down arrow, it skips over the block entirely. I want it to go into the       
  block. Same as when my keyboard cursor is below the block and I press the up  
  arrow. It works fine when I press the left or right arrow though.             
● The root problem is using Decoration.replace on the whole block — that removes
   the content from the editor's perspective, so the cursor has nowhere to land.
   The fix is to stop replacing the content entirely and instead:

  - Multi-line: use Decoration.line to style each line + Decoration.replace to
  hide only the 3-char """ delimiters (content text stays in the document, so
  arrow keys and clicks work normally)
  - Single-line: use Decoration.replace to hide the delimiters + Decoration.mark
   to style the content inline (same principle)

● Reload the plugin. Here's what changed and why it fixes both issues:

  Click to place cursor — the content text is no longer replaced by a widget, so
   a click maps to an actual document position naturally.

  Up/down arrow navigation — same reason: the lines exist in the document, so
  the cursor moves through them line by line. Only the """ delimiters (6 chars)
  are hidden, not the content.

  Visual appearance — the open/close lines look like thin strips (their only
  content was """ which is now hidden), forming the top and bottom edges of the
  box. Content lines get the background + left border.

  Edit mode — clicking anywhere inside the block puts the cursor inside
  [openIdx, closeEnd], which triggers the raw-text reveal so you can see and
  edit the """ syntax directly, same as before.

       87 +function emitHashFence(builder, doc, block) {                 
       88 +  const { openLine, closeLine } = block;                      
       89 +                                                              
       90 +  // Opening fence line: style it, then hide the "# ```" text.
       91 +  builder.add(openLine.from, openLine.from, Decoration.line({ 
          +class: 'hash-fence-open' }));                                 
       92 +  builder.add(openLine.from, openLine.to, Decoration.replace({
          +}));                                                          
       93 +                                                              
       94 +  // Content lines.                                           
       95 +  let pos = openLine.to + 1;                                  
       96 +  while (pos <= closeLine.from) {                             
       97 +    const line = doc.lineAt(pos);                             
       98 +    if (line.number < closeLine.number) {                     
       99 +      builder.add(line.from, line.from, Decoration.line({ clas
          +s: 'hash-fence-content' }));                                  
      100 +    }                                                         
      101 +    pos = line.to + 1;                                        
      102 +  }                                                           
      103 +                                                              
      104 +  // Closing fence line: style it, then hide the "# ```" text.
      105 +  builder.add(closeLine.from, closeLine.from, Decoration.line(
          +{ class: 'hash-fence-close' }));                              
      106 +  builder.add(closeLine.from, closeLine.to, Decoration.replace
          +({}));                                                        
      107 +}                                                             
      108 +                                                              
      109 +// ── Main builder ───────────────────────────────────────────
          +────────────────────                                          
      110 +                                                              
      111 +function buildDecorations(state) {                            
      112 +  const builder = new RangeSetBuilder();                      
      113 +  const doc    = state.doc;                                   
      114 +  const text   = doc.toString();                              
      115 +  const cursor = state.selection.main.head;                   
      116 +                                                              
      117 +  // Collect blocks from both syntaxes, merge in document orde
          +r.                                                            
      118 +  const blocks = [                                            
      119 +    ...collectTripleQuoteBlocks(text),                        
      120 +    ...collectHashFenceBlocks(doc),                           
      121 +  ].sort((a, b) => a.from - b.from);                          
      122 +                                                              
      123 +  for (const block of blocks) {                               
      124 +    // If cursor is inside this block, skip all decorations so
          + the raw syntax                                               
      125 +    // is visible and editable (mirrors Obsidian's bold/italic
          + behaviour).                                                  
      126 +    if (cursor > block.from && cursor < block.to) continue;   
      127 +                                                              
      128 +    if (block.type === 'triple-quote') {                      
      129 +      emitTripleQuote(builder, doc, text, block);             
      130 +    } else {                                                  
      131 +      emitHashFence(builder, doc, block);                     
      132 +    }                                                         
      133 +  }                                                           
      134 +                                                              
      135    return builder.finish();
      136  }

● Reload the plugin. Here's how the new syntax works:

  # ```
  code goes here
  # ```

  # ```gdscript
  func foo():
      pass
  # ```

  A few notes on the design:

  - Language tags are supported on the opening fence (# ```gdscript, # 
  ```python, etc.) and ignored on the close, matching standard markdown fence
  rules. The tag is detected but not used for highlighting — that would require
  a full language parser.
  - Cursor-inside edit mode works identically to the triple-quote blocks — move
  your cursor into the block and the raw # ```  syntax reappears.
  - Arrow key / click navigation works for the same reason as before — content
  lines are never replaced, only styled.
  - Ordering — both block types are collected first, sorted by document
  position, then decorations are emitted in one pass. This prevents
  RangeSetBuilder ordering violations if the two syntaxes ever appear
  interleaved.

● Reload the plugin. Summary of what changed:

  - Syntax: fences now require a leading space — # ``` (and  # ```gdscript,
  etc.)
  - Copy button: appears on the right side of the opening fence line. Clicking
  it copies the content between the fences to the clipboard and briefly shows
  "Copied!" before reverting. The button is absolutely positioned so it doesn't
  affect text layout.

  The content copied excludes the fence lines themselves — just the raw code
  between them, with no trailing newline.

✻ Baked for 4m 9s
